customer.business: NOCTIS, a smart bedside companion by offhours (EUR 120)
customer.target: Design-aware adults in Europe, 25 to 45, with disposable income, who scroll in bed and use their phone as alarm, and care about sleep and how their home looks

behaviours.name: Gadget sceptic

behaviours.name: Deal hunter
behaviours.how: Waits for discounts and compares prices across Amazon and brands.

behaviours.name: Sleep-curious
behaviours.how: Reads about sleep, owns a watch or ring, wary of health claims.

behaviours.name: Smart-home owner

objections: EUR 120 is a lot when my phone already does this for free
I already own an Echo or Nest that does alarm and weather
Will the alarm still work if the Wi-Fi is down

Does it listen to me all night, what about privacy

habits: you check your phone for about 30 minutes before falling asleep
your phone charges on the bedside table and is the first thing you look at in the morning
you use your phone alarm and snooze it more than once
you have thought about leaving the phone in another room but never did

pitch:
NOCTIS is a small timber bedside companion with a 4-inch square touch screen. It replaces your phone at the bedside so the phone can stay in another room.
It wakes you gradually with screen light, rising sound and a quiet haptic pulse, then gives a short spoken briefing: the weather, your first calendar event and how long until it, and an estimate of your sleep and snoring from room sensing. It is not a medical device and does not track sleep stages.
You can ask it a question out loud, such as "What is first today?" or "Wake me at 6:30." Microphone audio is processed on the device and conversations are not stored.
No subscription, no ads, no feed, no phone notifications. Setup and calendar connection happen once in a companion phone app.
Price: EUR 120. Available to pre-order on the waitlist at offhours.tech; first units are made in small batches.
